propositions: The T11 post-rollback schema state rule generates 8 of 21 sampled findings that are near-identical tautologies against append-only stores, drowning genuine data-loss risks.

The old unconditional post-rollback paragraph must be replaced with a four-condition applicability rule (interpretation change, in-place rewrite, read path removal, one-way transformation) that applies to all persistence technologies without naming store specifics.
Purely additive backward-compatible changes (new record types, optional fields, new tables with defaults) must be explicitly excluded from post-rollback findings via an anti-false-positive line.
The applicability rule and anti-FP guidance must be store-technology-agnostic so they apply equally to SQL, event stores, document databases, and config formats.
